purpose: Collect designated files from multiple VPS hosts into Cloudflare storage (R2 for file bodies, D1 for metadata) and let other devices download them by association.
requirements: Files at designated paths on multiple VPS hosts are collected into non-filesystem durable storage.
Other devices can discover and download those files.
Storage stack is Cloudflare Workers + D1 (metadata) + R2 (file bodies).
Synchronisation is scheduled, incremental, and content-hash deduplicated: only new or changed files are pushed.
Data flow is VPS-side agent push -> Worker ingest API -> R2 write -> D1 metadata write -> consumer download.
No multi-statement atomicity may be assumed on D1; use object-level atomicity, idempotent writes, and compensating actions.
constraints: Cloudflare Workers have no long-lived process and cannot open SSH/SFTP sessions, so the Worker cannot initiate collection; the VPS side must push.
The VPS-side agent runs on machines outside this repository's control; once the ingest API ships it must stay backward compatible.
Authorization: code writes, local commits, and pushes to a remote PR are allowed; deploying to VPS or mutating live Cloudflare resources is NOT authorized.
web_fetch is unavailable on this machine, so platform limits must never be asserted from memory.
Node/pnpm/Python are not on PATH; use DSH-bundled runtimes.
acceptance: A VPS-side agent can push a designated file and it becomes retrievable by a second device.
Re-running the sync with no file changes produces no new objects (idempotent, hash-deduplicated).
A changed file produces a new version while the previous version remains resolvable.
Metadata in D1 lets a consumer find a file by VPS/path without knowing the R2 object key.
Documented partial-failure and recovery behaviour for an interrupted push.
